transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, good day to you, sir! Welcome to the workshop of Master [Master's Name, I'll just use "the Master" for now, as I don't have a specific name]. How may I be of service? I must, however, regrettably inform you that the Master himself is presently away, visiting timber suppliers up north. He won't be back for several weeks, I'm afraid. Is there something I can assist you with in his stead? I handle most of the customer affairs and minor repairs when he's traveling.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Good day to you as well. It is indeed unfortunate that the Master is not present, but I must express my dissatisfaction with the custom fortepiano that was delivered to the Imperial Court's music room. The keys stick, the pedal mechanism is faulty, and the tone in the upper register is not up to the standard I expected. These issues must be rectified immediately. I demand that the necessary corrections be made promptly to ensure the quality of the instrument meets the expectations of the Imperial Court."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Ah, Maestro Salieri! Forgive my not recognizing you immediately, your reputation precedes you. I am deeply sorry to hear of these troubles with the fortepiano. That is certainly not the standard we strive for here at the Master's workshop.

However, regarding rectification, I must state quite clearly that all commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The Court’s own servants, if I recall correctly, signed the receipt confirming the instrument's arrival and initial inspection. Our guild rules, you see, strictly forbid reopening a completed commission without the Master’s personal approval. As I mentioned, he is away for several weeks. Without his direct instruction, my hands are tied in this matter of a full repair or replacement.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Your acknowledgement of my identity is duly noted. However, it is unacceptable that the instrument delivered to the Imperial Court in my name falls short of the standards expected. Guild rules or not, the reputation of both the Master and myself is at stake here. The Court's servants may have signed the receipt, but it is evident that the instrument is not in a state fit for use in such esteemed surroundings.

I insist that you take immediate action to address these issues. It is inconceivable that the Imperial Court should be left with a faulty fortepiano due to bureaucratic limitations. Inform the Master upon his return that I demand a personal audience to discuss this matter further. In the meantime, I expect you to do everything within your power to rectify these deficiencies promptly. Failure to do so will have consequences for both the workshop and its reputation.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro, I understand your concern for the reputation of the Imperial Court, and indeed, for our workshop's good name. It weighs heavily upon me to hear of your dissatisfaction. I assure you, if it were within my power, I would personally see to every detail.

However, "doing everything within my power" is precisely what I am constrained by. The guild's regulations are quite strict on this, as are the Master's own instructions. Reopening a completed commission, especially one of such magnitude for the Imperial Court, goes beyond the scope of a journeyman's authority without the Master's explicit consent. Any attempt on my part to undertake such a repair would be a breach of protocol and could result in severe penalties from the guild. It truly is a matter that only the Master can authorize upon his return.

I will, of course, inform him immediately upon his return of your insistence for a personal audience, and convey every detail of your displeasure. I will emphasize the urgency and the importance of the matter. But for now, Maestro, I truly regret that I am unable to proceed with the requested repairs or replacement without the Master's direct approval. My hands are tied by these established rules.

transcript.text:
I appreciate your dedication to adhering to the regulations set forth by the guild and the Master's instructions. However, the urgency of the situation cannot be overstated. The musical integrity of the Imperial Court is of paramount importance, and any delay in addressing these issues could have far-reaching consequences.

I urge you to convey to the Master the gravity of the situation upon his return. Emphasize the pressing need for his personal attention to rectify the flaws in the instrument. Stress the significance of maintaining the Court's musical standards and the honor associated with providing a flawless fortepiano for our esteemed musicians to use.

I trust that the Master will recognize the importance of this matter and take swift action to ensure that the instrument is brought up to the standards befitting the Imperial Court. I eagerly await his return and the resolution of these pressing concerns.

Maestro Salieri, you have my solemn word. I shall convey your message with every ounce of emphasis and detail you have expressed. I will impress upon the Master the precise gravity of the situation, the urgency, and the paramount importance of the Imperial Court's musical integrity. I will ensure he understands the full weight of your expectations for a swift and satisfactory resolution.

I only wish I could offer you more immediate comfort or action, but rest assured, the moment the Master steps back into this workshop, your concerns will be the very first matter brought to his attention. We pride ourselves on our craft, and it pains us to hear of any dissatisfaction from such a respected patron.

Until then, Maestro, I thank you for your patience and understanding of the limitations I currently face. I will be sure to send word to you the very moment the Master returns.
